content.punchline: A hybrid three-strategy framework turns six targets into concrete per-patient cocktail drafts for 61% of a real cohort

slides.speaker_notes_seed: Bridge from S2: six Tier-A pathobionts are now in hand, externally replicated. The question S3 answers is whether those targets can translate into a concrete clinical intervention. The punchline is yes — but with an honest pivot: three of the six highest-scored targets have no lytic phage, so a pure phage cocktail is structurally infeasible for the dominant E1 ecotype. The deck closes on what IS achievable: a hybrid 3-strategy framework that gives concrete cocktail drafts to 61% of a real UC Davis patient cohort, plus state-dependent dosing rules grounded in a longitudinal trajectory observation.

content.title: Methods: 3-layer phage-evidence stack assesses targetability across 6 Tier-A candidates, then NB15 + NB16 build per-patient cocktail drafts
bullets: NB12 — curated literature foundation: 12 organisms × phage-availability scoring (0–3); stratifies Tier-A into 4 classes: clinical-trial-stage, lytic-literature, temperate-only, GAP

NB13 — PhageFoundry quantitative cocktail design: 96 phages × 188 E. coli strains × 17,672 experimentally-tested susceptibility pairs; greedy minimum-set-cover finds smallest cocktail covering ≥95% of strains
NB14 — in-vivo HMP2 phageome correlation: per-phage-family correlation with Tier-A abundance in HMP2 samples; validates in-vivo phage presence for E. coli (Podoviridae +0.18, Myoviridae +0.13)

NB15 — per-patient cocktail draft: 23 UC Davis CD patients × per-patient profile (ecotype + Montreal + calprotectin + medication + Kuehl_WGS Tier-A presence); apply Pillar-4 hand-off framework to produce concrete per-patient cocktail components

NB16 — longitudinal stability: patient 6967 (the only multi-timepoint patient with biological-replicate samples) tests cocktail drift across ecotype transitions; NB16 §5 derives state-dependent dosing rules
NB17 — cross-cutting synthesis: per-patient master table + target decision matrix (6 Tier-A × 5 attributes) + 4-phase clinical-translation roadmap

slides.speaker_notes_seed: Walk through all three phage-evidence layers before revealing the cocktail. Layer 1 (NB12) is qualitative but load-bearing: it is the only layer that covers all 6 Tier-A species, and it is where the GAP classification for H. hathewayi and F. plautii originates. Layer 2 (NB13) is quantitative but E. coli-only: the 96 × 188 × 17,672 susceptibility matrix is the most rigorous piece of the stack. Layer 3 (NB14) is corroborative: in-vivo phage correlation validates that the E. coli phage signal is ecologically real, not just a lab artifact. NB15 and NB16 are the clinical-translation layer that turns the phage-targetability framework into per-patient deliverables. Emphasize the honest limitation: NB12 has no experimental susceptibility data for the 5 non-E. coli species — PhageFoundry is E. coli-only. Source: REPORT.md §Pillar 4 deliverables (NB12/NB13/NB14) + §22-23 (NB15/NB16).

step_caption: Each Tier-A target is classified by NB12 phage-availability tier; patients may carry 2–5 targets depending on ecotype + carriage profile
Three design strategies are matched to phage class: direct lytic phage for E. coli/E. bolteae/E. lenta, non-phage alternatives for GAP species, engineering/biochemical for M. gnavus
Per-patient hybrid cocktail blends all applicable strategies; pure phage cocktail is structurally infeasible for any E1 patient (all 9 E1 carry at least 2 GAP/temperate species)

slides.speaker_notes_seed: This slide covers A9 (✓ direct) and A10 (✓ direct). The 3-strategy framework is verbatim from REPORT §Pillar 4 closure synthesis: '(1) direct phage targeting (E. coli AIEC + E. bolteae PMBT24 + E. lenta PMBT5), (2) alternative therapies (H. hathewayi GAG-degrading enzyme inhibitors; F. plautii BA-binding co-therapy), (3) limited/engineered (M. gnavus lytic-locked phage engineering or biochemical glucorhamnan-synthesis target).' Principle 1 from REPORT §Pillar 5 closure synthesis: 'Pure phage cocktail is structurally infeasible for the dominant E1 ecotype. All 9 E1 patients carry the full 5-species Tier-A pathobiont module, but only 3 of the 5 species have direct lytic phage options. The remaining 2 (H. hathewayi, F. plautii) are Pillar-4 GAP species.' Stress to audience: this is an honest finding — the framework cannot be a pure phage cocktail, and it doesn't pretend to be. The clinical-translation deliverable is the hybrid framework + templates, not a ready-to-deploy cocktail. Transition: so what fraction of patients actually get a concrete draft from this framework?

content.title: Patient 6967's E1→E3 drift is consistent with ecotype-dynamic dosing — a universal trio anchors the cocktail backbone across states
bullets: Patient 6967 shows E1→E3 ecotype drift with M. gnavus 14× expansion (0.53→7.45 reads) as dominant signature; cocktail Jaccard between visits = 0.60 — moderate overlap, not a complete rewrite (n=1 trajectory; ecotype call confidences 0.64 / 0.41)
Three species span both ecotype states: M. gnavus + H. hathewayi + E. lenta constitute the universal Tier-1 trio — cocktail backbone for any active-disease CD patient regardless of ecotype

Five state-dependent dosing rules follow (Novel Contribution #24): F. plautii inclusion is E1-specific; E. coli inclusion is E3-specific; M. gnavus qPCR 5-fold change as a candidate proxy for triggering full ecotype re-test — preliminary evidence only, not a validated assay

slides.speaker_notes_seed: This slide covers A12 (⚠ partial — n=1 longitudinal trajectory; ecotype call confidence moderate; M. gnavus qPCR threshold is a hypothesis, not validated). The language is deliberately hedged per the partial-analysis discipline. Key numbers verbatim from REPORT §NB16: 'M. gnavus 14× expansion (0.53 → 7.45 reads)'; 'Cocktail Jaccard (visit 1 × visit 2) = 0.60'; ecotype call confidence '0.64' and '0.41'; 'Patient 1112 technical replicate Spearman ρ = 1.000 (p < 0.001)' validates Kaiju reliability. The 5 state-dependent dosing rules are REPORT §NB16 §5 verbatim: (a) re-test ecotype every 3-6 months; (b) F. plautii inclusion E1-specific; (c) E. coli inclusion E3-specific; (d) universal Tier-1 trio is backbone; (e) M. gnavus qPCR as cheap clinical proxy. REPORT explicitly flags: '5-fold change in M. gnavus abundance might be the threshold for triggering full ecotype re-evaluation' — the 'might' is the author's word, not just our caution. Caveat to name aloud: n=1 trajectory means these rules are biologically motivated hypotheses, not clinically validated guidelines. Multi-cohort longitudinal validation is flagged in the NB17 roadmap as near-term priority.
